trust_decision.summary: Whether a sitemap-capable user may change a page's display order is decided only by the global canAccessSitemap() gate (no per-page move_or_copy_page check, no CSRF token) in the backend sitemap_update controller and the dashboard explore single page.

fix_sites.entry_point: ANY /ccm/system/backend/dashboard/sitemap_update (concrete/routes/backend/dashboard.php:22); fix adds CSRF token validation (fix.diff:256-260)
same route; cID[] from POST body or query string (sitemap_update.php:44); fix adds per-page canMoveOrCopyPage and check-all-then-apply (fix.diff:268-282)

GET/POST /dashboard/sitemap/explore?task=send_to_top|send_to_bottom&cNodeID=N (links built in concrete/js/cms.js:11); fix adds task allow-list, int cast, existence and canMoveOrCopyPage (fix.diff:1192-1200)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: concrete/controllers/single_page/dashboard/sitemap/explore.php:27-36 (send_to_top/send_to_bottom via Page::movePageDisplayOrderToTop/Bottom, concrete/src/Page/Page.php:3427-3454), a separate reorder implementation in another controller tree

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names SitemapUpdate::updateDisplayOrder only; the Flat View 'send to top/bottom' is a different page, a different Page API (movePageDisplayOrderToTop/Bottom) and a plain GET navigation link, so it looks like a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reordering a page legitimately renumbers all of its siblings (movePageDisplayOrderToTop and movePageDisplayOrderToSibling call updateDisplayOrder on each sibling), and the drag_request move/copy/alias flow reorders via the same primitive. A fix that puts the per-page check in Page::updateDisplayOrder or requires move permission on every sibling breaks send-to-top and drag-and-drop for users with move rights on only one page. Requiring a token on explore without changing the tokenless GET links in cms.js breaks the Flat View menu.

O6_input_shapes: cID[] array in the POST body (sitemap_update.php:44)
cID[] array in the query string, a GET fallback (sitemap_update.php:44)
mixed list where some IDs are allowed and some are not: the fix checks every page before applying any change (all-or-nothing, fix.diff:268-282)
non-existent or error page IDs are skipped (sitemap_update.php:65-66)
explore: task/cNodeID from POST or query string (explore.php:19-26); non-numeric cNodeID cast to int, unknown task values rejected (fix.diff:1192-1196)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Flat View send_to_top/send_to_bottom still changes state on a GET with no CSRF token after the fix (the fix adds a token only to sitemap_update), so the CWE-352 half stays open on this route for pages the victim may move.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a navigation link (cms.js:11 builds a tokenless href) on a dashboard page, and the published fix itself left it without a token, so a solver can argue the per-page permission check is enough.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different controller tree (controllers/single_page vs controllers/backend), linked from a compiled JS bundle

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling backend endpoint (for example sitemap sort-to-sibling) calling Page::movePageDisplayOrderToSibling with only the canRead() gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sitemap_check_in and sitemap_update already sit here with the same coarse Sitemap::canRead gate; a maintainer adding drag-sort without the drag_request dialog would copy that pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a public Page helper or REST API action (concrete/src/Api/Controller/Pages.php) that takes a cID list and calls updateDisplayOrder($order, $cID) for another page's ID
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: updateDisplayOrder already accepts a foreign $cID by design (Page.php:3382-3391), so a batch wrapper at the API layer would reach any page without a per-page Checker.

O9_family: missing per-object authorization (IDOR) plus missing CSRF token on a state-changing route

O10_build.project_tests: tests/tests/Application/UserInterface/Sitemap/SitemapTest.php exists; no tests for SitemapUpdate or Explore reorder. Behavioural tests need an installed site with DB, users and page permissions.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add canMoveOrCopyPage inside the sitemap_update loop (skip or throw mid-loop, so reordering is partly applied) and leave the explore send_to_top/bottom route and the CSRF token untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit is the omnibus 9.5.3 release (about 115 files: XSS, SQL casts, unserialize, validation-hash type, block process, API controllers); only 2 files belong to this advisory.

drag_request move/copy/alias also reorders via movePageDisplayOrderToSibling but already validates a token and canMoveOrCopyPage (concrete/controllers/dialog/page/drag_request.php:56-60; concrete/src/Page/Sitemap/DragRequestData.php:420).
